findings.claim: A publisher can rename the head after the case lock file has been replaced. The pre-rename callback validates the lock before reading the head and never validates it again after that read.
findings.repro: Start with two entries. During the third append, intercept the pre-rename _read_head call with raise_os=True. Read and retain the old head, replace the case lock file, then return the retained head. The comparison succeeds, the head rename proceeds and the append returns entry 3 as recorded. P15 requires the rename to be refused, the save to report not recorded, and entry 3 to remain past the recorded head. The same helper performs take-back renames.

findings.claim: An interruption after read-back fails can still bypass take-back. Moving the call into finally handles exceptions raised during the read-back body, but the call itself remains interruptible before take-back starts.
findings.repro: Append entry 3 to a two-entry log. Make LogCheck.ok raise KeyboardInterrupt when checking the published three-entry head, as the existing test does. Also inject KeyboardInterrupt at the line event for the call to _take_back in the finally block. The caller receives SaveNotConfirmed and a fresh check shows entry 3 recorded. The writer still held the case, its head was unchanged and no take-back was attempted. The runner test injects only the first interruption.

findings.claim: The producer's CLI contract claim gives the wrong exit code and wording for a torn tail while another writer holds the case.
findings.repro: Read the passed contracts-4.log result for test_case_check_while_another_writer_appends_reports_the_recorded_log_not_a_break and compare its assertions with the claim. The test requires exit 4 and 'being saved'. The claim says exit 0 and 'appending'. The implementation follows P15 on this path.

findings.claim: The rapid-append test passed, but it does not prove the producer's claim that it reproduced two commits on every retry followed by a contended fallback.
findings.repro: Inspect the test's background loop and assertions. It runs 40 checks against an unsynchronized writer and asserts that none names a bad entry. It neither counts commits per attempt nor ensures the fallback lock is contended. To prove that exact schedule, add a synchronized test that forces both conditions, then run python -m pytest -v tests/test_case_log.py -k 'healthy_log_broken'.
